title: FPS — Intermediate
summary: The Project JOHNO first-person kit: an L2 modifier and radial menus, GASP gait, area of interest, ballistics with heat, limb medical at a 10% floor, slots, a ten-slot gunsmith, and a save.

sections.title: L2 input and radial menus
sections.why: The L2 layer remaps the button. The graph still starts at the action.
reading: Project JOHNO does not put every FPS binding in one mapping context. Move, look, fire, and interact live on the base context. Holding the left trigger pushes a second context, the L2 modifier layer. A face button that reloads on the base layer can open a radial slot while that layer is up. The event graph never reads the trigger itself. Enhanced Input has already turned the key, the trigger, or the stick sector into an action by the time Triggered fires.

In UE5 the player controller or the possessed pawn adds the base mapping context when the pawn is possessed. The L2 action is a chord or a trigger on its own input action. While it is held, AddMappingContext pushes the modifier context at a higher priority. Release pops it. The radial menu is a widget that reports a sector as an input action value, usually IA_Equip, not as a line trace. The menu does not simulate the pawn.

The figure is the interact graph because that is the action this layer still has to honor. IA_Interact sits at the left. Triggered feeds the line trace. The hit bool is the branch. The true pin calls Interact through ProcessEvent. Nothing in that chain changes when the binding moves from a keyboard key to a pad button on the L2 layer. If the radial menu is what the player opened, the action name is different and the gunsmith graph runs instead.

The efficient shape pushes one context on press and pops it on release. Polling the trigger inside Tick, and rebuilding the key map every frame, fights the chord Enhanced Input already evaluated. A radial menu that line-traces to see where the stick points is the same mistake: the stick is an axis, and the sector is math on that axis. Movement must keep IA_Move from the base context while L2 is held, so the modifier layer adds actions. It does not replace move. The jammer, if the kit has EW gear, is another action on that layer. Destruction does not read input. It listens for the damage event later.

The figure is the real Interact graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. IA_Interact fires when the player presses the interact key. Keep the key on the input action, not in this graph. A short line trace from the camera. Hit is true when something solid is in front of the player. Only talk to an actor when the trace hit. A miss should do nothing expensive. Call Interact through an interface. The door, the chest, and the switch can all answer. A The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 10 is `FHitResult Hit_tpl_interact_trace; bool bHit_tpl_interact_trace = false; if (UWorld* World_tpl_interact_trace `. Line 13 is `if (AActor* Target_tpl_interact_call = Cast<AActor>(Hit_tpl_interact_trace.GetActor())) { if (UFunction* Fn_tp`.

Across this track, keep Enhanced Input, L2 modifier, IA_Interact, Radial menu distinct. The L2 layer remaps the button. The graph still starts at the action. The L2 modifier layer is the second mapping context. The radial menu sends IA_Equip. The interact graph still starts at IA_Interact.

sections.title: GASP movement
sections.why: Motion matching reads the gait. The graph only writes Speed.
reading: GASP, the Game Animation Sample motion-matching setup, chooses a pose from the speed and the gait the pawn is already in. It does not decide that speed. The movement graph does. IA_Move arrives as an axis. Greater than zero selects the sprint literal, 600. The released axis selects the walk literal, 200. Those two writes are the whole contract the animation database needs.

UE5 character movement consumes MaxWalkSpeed, which this sample stores as Speed. Motion matching queries a trajectory built from that speed and from the acceleration the movement component already has. A second line trace inside the anim blueprint, fired on Tick to discover whether the player is walking, repeats work the input graph finished. The database wants a number, not a hit result.

Read the generated function. The branch is if ((IA_Move > 0.f)). The true body assigns Speed = 600.f. The else assigns Speed = 200.f. There is no Tick override in the excerpt. Putting the same assignments in Tick would stomp a stance an ability had just set, and the motion-matching query would blend toward a gait the player had already left.

The weapon, the aim, and the camera all ride the pawn this speed drives. They do not write Speed. A vehicle later in a wider kit has its own throttle graph and must not reuse this component's Speed, or the on-foot database and the wheel speed fight. Save can store the gait if a mode needs it. It should not store the animation pose. The pose is derived.

The figure is the real Movement graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. IA_Move is the axis. The character movement component consumes Speed. Zero axis means the stick is released. Greater than zero means the player is pushing move. A live axis takes the fast path. A released axis walks. Sprint speed. Walk speed. Write sprint speed. Write walk speed. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 9 is `Speed = 600.f; // node:tpl_movement_sprint`. Line 13 is `Speed = 200.f; // node:tpl_movement_walk`.

Across this track, keep IA_Move, Speed, GASP, Motion matching distinct. Motion matching reads the gait. The graph only writes Speed. if ((IA_Move > 0.f)) chooses Speed = 600.f or Speed = 200.f. Tick does not assign Speed. GASP reads the result.

sections.title: Area of interest
sections.why: The server decides Relevant on a timer, not on Tick.
reading: Area of interest is how a large FPS stops shipping every actor to every client. Project JOHNO's netcode note is the same rule: relevance is a server fact. A pawn across the map is not replicated just because its widget exists. The sample graph stands in for that test. Begin Play starts a timer. Twice a second, CheckAOI runs, the authority traces, and Relevant is set from the hit.

UE5's replication graph is the production version of this timer. It groups actors by cell and by team. The sample cannot build that graph in one event, so it uses a line trace as the stand-in and writes a bool. The interval in the generated timer is 0.5f, looping. That is a relevancy pass, not a render pass. Clients that are not relevant never receive the actor's properties.

The excerpt shows SetTimer for Graph_CheckAOI at 0.5f, then HasAuthority, then the trace, then Relevant = bHit. The authority if in the sample is an empty block before the trace. Read that as a defect to repair: the relevance write has to sit inside the authority, or a client can mark itself relevant and pull actors the server meant to hide. The widget is never the replicated object.

Interaction, the weapon, and health still run for a relevant pawn. They do not each run their own relevancy test. EW gear that listens for signals should use the same relevance gate, or a jammer across the map costs bandwidth for a noise nobody can hear. Destruction debris should die out of relevance quickly. A Tick that asks every connection about every actor is the failure mode this timer replaces.

The figure is the real Area of interest graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. Begin Play starts the relevance timer. Relevance is checked twice a second, not every frame. CheckAOI is the relevancy pass. The server decides who is relevant. A stand-in for distance. A real AOI uses the replication graph. Relevant gates replication. The widget is not replicated. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 10 is `if (UWorld* World = GetWorld()) { FTimerHandle Timer_tpl_aoi_timer; World->GetTimerManager().SetTimer(Timer_tp`. Line 15 is `if (HasAuthority()) { /* authority */ } // node:tpl_aoi_auth`.

Across this track, keep CheckAOI, Has Authority, Relevant, Replication graph distinct. The server decides Relevant on a timer, not on Tick. SetTimer calls CheckAOI at 0.5f. Relevant = bHit, inside HasAuthority. Tick is not the pass.

sections.title: Ballistics, wear, and heat
sections.why: A shot traces once and adds heat. Wear is state on the weapon.
reading: A Project JOHNO shot is one event. IA_Fire starts it. The trace is the sample projectile. Wear and heat are state on the weapon component, updated because a shot happened, not because a frame happened. Heat climbs by a small step. Wear is the same kind of number, stored beside heat, and a data asset should own how much one shot adds. The graph does not spawn a bullet actor per pellet.

UE5 can represent the projectile as this line trace or as a physical projectile spawned from the same action. Either way the action is the start. The generated function traces with LineTraceSingleByChannel on the visibility channel, then branches on bHit. The true body adds heat: Heat = (Heat + 0.05f). A miss in this sample adds nothing, which is the simplification to know about. A real barrel still heats on a miss. The lesson's repair is to add heat on the action, and apply damage only on the hit.

Wear uses the same write pattern as heat, with its own float, and it should clamp before the weapon data says the barrel is ruined. Replicating every pellet's transform is the expensive version. Replicating heat and wear as two floats, from the authority, is the cheap one. Clients play the flash locally from the fire action. They do not invent the damage.

The magazine graph still owns Magazine and Reserve. This graph should not decrement them, or a reload and a shot will disagree. Health receives damage from the hit, through the damage event, and does not read Heat. The gunsmith asset can name the heat step per barrel. Save stores heat and wear with the equipped id. A vehicle cannon is a different fire event. It should not reuse this Heat float.

The figure is the real Ballistics graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. IA_Fire is the shot. Wear and heat update here. The trace is the sample projectile. A physical projectile would replace this node, not Tick. A hit applies damage. A miss still adds heat. Heat plus a step. Current heat. One shot of heat. Write heat on the weapon component. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 10 is `FHitResult Hit_tpl_ballistics_trace; bool bHit_tpl_ballistics_trace = false; if (UWorld* World_tpl_ballistics_`. Line 13 is `Heat = (Heat + 0.05f); // node:tpl_ballistics_set`.

Across this track, keep IA_Fire, Line trace, Heat, Wear distinct. A shot traces once and adds heat. Wear is state on the weapon. IA_Fire starts the shot. The excerpt does Heat = (Heat + 0.05f) on a hit. Tick and per-pellet actors go away. Damage stays on the hit. Heat should also rise on a miss.

sections.title: Limb medical and the 10% clamp
sections.why: The server writes the float. A limb does not fall below 10% from a normal hit.
reading: Project JOHNO treats a body as attributes, not as one bar only. A limb has its own float. A normal hit may drop that limb, but not through the floor the design set: 10% of the limb's max. The clamp is the rule. The sample graph is the replicated health graph, because the networking rule is the same whether the float is named Health or LeftArm. Any Damage arrives. Only the authority writes. Clients hear OnRep.

The generated function is Graph_AnyDamage. It tests HasAuthority in an empty block, then assigns Health = 90.f. That 90 is the sample literal standing in for a computed result. Read the empty block as the bug the medical kit has to close: the assignment must be inside the authority test, and the value must be the clamped result, not a literal typed on the client. A limb at 100 with a max of 100 does not go to 0 from a bruise. The floor is 0.1 times max. A dedicated downed state, not this clamp, is what crosses zero.

OnRep_Health in the excerpt logs that health changed. That is the client notify. A hit flash, a limp, or a blood widget belongs there. Subtracting again inside OnRep double-applies the hit. The limb widget reads the float. It is not replicated.

Ballistics calls this damage event. It does not write the limb. The gunsmith does not. Save stores the limb floats after the authority has written them. A medic item in the inventory calls the same event with a negative damage, still on the authority, and the same clamp keeps the limb at or under its max. EW and vehicles do not own limbs. A destroyed vehicle is a different health component.

The figure is the real Replicated health graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. Any Damage is the request. Authority decides. Has Authority keeps the change on the server. A stand-in for health after the hit. Set the replicated health. OnRep runs on the clients that hear the property. The UI listens. It does not decide the number. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 9 is `if (HasAuthority()) { /* authority */ } // node:tpl_replicated-health_auth`. Line 10 is `Health = 90.f; // node:tpl_replicated-health_set`.

Across this track, keep Any Damage, Has Authority, OnRep, Limb clamp distinct. The server writes the float. A limb does not fall below 10% from a normal hit. Nest the write inside if (HasAuthority()). A normal hit clamps the limb to 10% of its max. OnRep only notifies.

assignment.prompt: The excerpt assigns Health = 90.f outside an empty HasAuthority block. Where must that write move, and what floor does a limb use?
assignment.model: Nest the write inside if (HasAuthority()). A normal hit clamps the limb to 10% of its max. OnRep only notifies.

sections.title: Inventory slots
sections.why: Overlap asks the interface. The slot owns the count.
reading: The FPS inventory is the slot that accepts a pickup. Overlap is the event. The generated function tests if ((StackCount > 0.f)). The true path finds AddToSlot on the other actor and calls it with ProcessEvent. The false path writes StackCount = 0.f. That is a sample, not a cap. A real slot compares the count with the stack size from the data asset before it accepts another item. The pickup does not write the slot variable itself.

UE5 overlap gives the other actor. The cast to AActor and the FindFunction lookup are the interface in the excerpt, because this sample resolves the function by name. A Blueprint interface with Execute_AddToSlot is the same contract once the project names it. A cast to one pickup class would exclude the medkit when the graph was written for a magazine.

Scanning every actor on Tick to find pickups repeats the overlap the physics scene already reported. The slot graph stays on the overlap. Interaction's line trace can highlight a pickup. It does not increment StackCount. The increment belongs here, after the cap check you add beside the sample's greater-than-zero test.

The weapon reads Reserve, which a stack of ammunition can fill by calling into the magazine graph. It does not reach into StackCount. The gunsmith id says which item the slot represents. Save writes the count. Health does not. A client that increments StackCount locally will snap back if the count is replicated, so the add runs where the slot's authority lives.

The figure is the real Inventory slot graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. Begin Overlap is the item touching the pawn. Read the stack the component already owns. Zero means the slot is empty. Greater asks if the stack is above zero. Branch before the interface call. Call the interface. Do not cast. The else path keeps the current count. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 12 is `if (AActor* Target_tpl_inventoryslot_call = Cast<AActor>(OtherActor)) { if (UFunction* Fn_tpl_inventoryslot_ca`. Line 16 is `StackCount = 0.f; // node:tpl_inventory-slot_store`.

Across this track, keep Overlap, StackCount, AddToSlot distinct. Overlap asks the interface. The slot owns the count. Compare StackCount with the data-asset stack size. A stack of ammo fills Reserve. The trace does not increment the slot.

sections.title: Ten-slot gunsmith
sections.why: Ten slots stay in the data asset. EquippedId is what replicates.
reading: The Project JOHNO gunsmith is a data record with ten slots. A slot holds an attachment id: optic, magazine, barrel, and the rest. The graph does not store transforms. IA_Equip selects a slot. The authority writes EquippedId. The owning client builds the visible weapon from the data asset that id names. A radial menu and a number key both send IA_Equip. The graph cannot tell them apart, and it should not try.

The excerpt is short. Graph_IA_Equip tests HasAuthority in an empty block, then assigns EquippedId = IA_Equip. The empty block is the same defect as the health sample: the assignment has to nest inside the check, or a client predicts an id the server will overwrite, and the mesh pops. The ten slot records never travel as actors. They live in the asset.

Spawning ten components on every equip replicates sockets the client can read from the asset. That is the expensive version. One id is the cheap version. Wear and heat from the ballistics graph hang off the equipped weapon, not off each slot. Swapping the id does not reset another player's limb medical state.

Inventory stores the weapon item that points at the same asset. Save stores EquippedId, not the meshes. Movement and GASP do not read it, except that a heavy weapon might change Speed through an ability, which is a different write. The L2 radial menu is just another sender of IA_Equip.

The figure is the real Gunsmith graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. IA_Equip picks a slot. The radial menu can send the same action. The server decides the equipped id. Replicate EquippedId. The client builds the mesh from the data asset. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 7 is `if (HasAuthority()) { /* authority */ } // node:tpl_gunsmith_auth`. Line 8 is `EquippedId = IA_Equip; // node:tpl_gunsmith_set`.

Across this track, keep IA_Equip, EquippedId, Ten slots distinct. Ten slots stay in the data asset. EquippedId is what replicates. EquippedId = IA_Equip, nested inside HasAuthority. The data record holds ten slots. The client builds meshes.

sections.title: Save the kit
sections.why: Begin Play loads one struct. Tick does not write it.
reading: The intermediate FPS save packs the values the other lessons own: Health or the limb floats, Heat, wear, Magazine, Reserve, StackCount, and EquippedId. Begin Play loads them, because the components exist. A Make struct is the sample's pack step. Set SlotValue stores the packed number. LoadSlot reads it back and Break pulls fields out. Input assets, the L2 context, and the GASP pose are not in the struct. They are derived or they are project data.

The excerpt's Begin Play builds an FVector, sets X to 1.f, and assigns SlotValue = 1.f. LoadSlot default-constructs an FHitResult and logs Loaded. Those types are the sample struct stand-ins. The lesson is the shape: one write, on an event, and a load from Begin Play. A Tick that assigns SlotValue from Health every frame hitches and stores a half-finished magazine.

Two slot indexes, autosave and manual, share the struct. They do not share a tick. The authority writes the gameplay numbers before the pack runs, or the slot stores a client guess. AOI relevance is not saved. It is recomputed from positions after load.

Destruction state, if a wall can be gone, is a separate list of ids in the same struct, not a mesh. EW gear charge is another float beside heat. A vehicle's throttle is not part of the on-foot slot. Load must run after the components exist, which is why Begin Play is the caller and not the constructor.

The figure is the real Save / load slot graph, with that preset's node positions and wires. Begin Play writes the slot once. Do not write it from Tick. The member written into the payload. Make Struct builds the save payload. Keep the member on the component. Load is its own event. It does not run during the save. Break Struct reads one member. A print stands in for the load UI. The C++ beside the figure is the compiler output for this same graph. Line 8 is `FVector Made_tpl_saveload_make = FVector::ZeroVector; Made_tpl_saveload_make.X = 1.f; Made_tpl_saveload_make.Y`. Line 9 is `SlotValue = 1.f; // node:tpl_save-load_store`.

Across this track, keep Begin Play, Make struct, LoadSlot, SlotValue distinct. Begin Play loads one struct. Tick does not write it. Begin Play loads. EquippedId belongs in the struct. The pose and the mapping context do not.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Tick should write SlotValue so a crash loses nothing.
quiz.why: A tick save hitches and stores a half-finished magazine.

quiz.prompt: What does LoadSlot do in the excerpt?
choices: Builds a break stand-in and logs Loaded
quiz.why: The break is the read path.

quiz.prompt: Why is AOI relevance not saved?
choices: It is recomputed from positions after load
quiz.why: Relevance follows from where actors are.

quiz.prompt: A destroyed wall belongs in the struct as what?
quiz.why: The id is enough to hide the wall again.

quiz.prompt: When must the authority write Health relative to the pack?
quiz.why: The slot should store the server number.

questions.prompt: Project JOHNO holds the left trigger. Which mapping context should be pushed?
choices: A Tick poll of the trigger
questions.why: L2 is a second context.

questions.prompt: The radial menu line-traces every frame to pick a sector. What should it send instead?
questions.why: The sector is an input value.

questions.prompt: True or false: the L2 layer should remove IA_Move while it is held.
questions.why: Move stays on the base context.

questions.prompt: GASP is blending to a sprint the player already cancelled. Which assignment was left on Tick?
questions.why: Speed belongs on IA_Move.

questions.prompt: The broken GASP graph writes Speed from the red Tick node. Which comparison should choose 600.f or 200.f?
questions.why: The axis owns the gait.

questions.prompt: A client sets Relevant true and actors pop in across the map. Which check was an empty block?
questions.why: Relevance is a server write.

questions.prompt: Tick forces Relevant true. What does the real excerpt do instead?
choices: SetTimer calls CheckAOI at 0.5f and assigns Relevant = bHit
questions.why: The timer is the relevancy pass.

questions.prompt: Heat climbs while the player is not firing. Where was the add left?
choices: On Tick, instead of Heat = (Heat + 0.05f) inside IA_Fire
questions.why: Heat steps on the shot.

questions.prompt: True or false: a miss should still heat the barrel, while damage waits for the hit.
questions.why: The sample only adds heat on a hit. The barrel does not care.

questions.prompt: A limb at max 100 falls to 0 from a bruise. Which floor was skipped?
questions.why: The clamp is the medical rule.

questions.prompt: The broken limb graph writes Health from Tick. Which event should start the write, and who gates it?
questions.why: Damage is the event. The server writes.

questions.prompt: OnRep subtracts Amount for a limb. The excerpt's OnRep only logs a change. What should the notify do?
choices: Play the limp and leave the float alone
questions.why: The server already wrote the clamped value.

questions.prompt: AddToSlot runs from a Tick scan of every actor. Which event does the excerpt use?
questions.why: Overlap is the pickup.

questions.prompt: Ten meshes replicate when the radial menu changes slot. What should the authority assign?
questions.why: The id selects the asset.

questions.prompt: EquippedId is assigned outside an empty HasAuthority block. What is the repair?
choices: Nest EquippedId = IA_Equip inside the authority check
Delete the id and replicate meshes
questions.why: The server owns the equipped record.

questions.prompt: SlotValue changes every frame and a crash restores half a magazine. Which call loads a finished struct?
choices: Begin Play, after the authority has written the floats
questions.why: Begin Play loads. Tick does not pack.

questions.prompt: The broken save graph writes the slot from Tick. Which node in the real graph packs a stand-in value at Begin Play?
questions.why: The sample packs on Begin Play.

questions.prompt: EW gear replicates its radio mesh to players who cannot hear it. Which bool should gate that actor?
questions.why: Out of interest, the jammer is not replicated.

questions.prompt: A vehicle cannon writes the rifle's Heat float. What should it use instead?
choices: Its own heat on the vehicle weapon
questions.why: The floats are different components.

questions.prompt: True or false: destruction debris should keep replicating after it leaves the interest cell.
questions.why: Debris dies out of relevance.

questions.prompt: The magazine clamp and the heat add both run. Which one owns Magazine?
choices: The reload graph's Clamp of Reserve into the gap
questions.why: Reload moves rounds. Ballistics does not.

questions.prompt: Motion matching stutters because a trace in the anim blueprint runs every frame. What number should it read?
questions.why: GASP reads the gait the movement graph wrote.

questions.prompt: A designer wants the heat step tunable per barrel. Where does it live?
choices: The weapon data asset selected by EquippedId
questions.why: The asset names the step. The graph adds it.

questions.prompt: The broken ballistics graph adds heat from Tick. Which action starts the real trace?
questions.why: Fire is the shot.

questions.prompt: Health = 90.f is the sample literal. For a limb max of 80, a normal hit cannot go below what?
questions.why: Ten percent of 80 is 8.

questions.prompt: The heat add was copied into Tick. Where does the excerpt put Heat = (Heat + 0.05f)?
choices: Inside Graph_IA_Fire, on the hit branch
questions.why: The shot function owns the add.

questions.prompt: Two save indexes exist, autosave and manual. What do they share?
choices: The struct layout, not a tick
questions.why: Both indexes use the same fields.

questions.prompt: A medic item writes the limb on the client so the bar moves early. What snaps?
choices: The server float, when it replicates
questions.why: The authority is the writer.

questions.prompt: True or false: EquippedId, Heat, and the limb floats are worth packing, and the animation pose is not.
questions.why: The pose is derived from Speed and the database.

questions.prompt: IA_Interact still traces after the binding moves from a key to a pad on the L2 layer. Why does the graph stay valid?
choices: The graph starts at the action, not at the key
The trace reads the mapping context
questions.why: Enhanced Input resolves the binding first.
